headline: Axion 1.0: Open Agent Foundation Models, Simplified
tldr: Axion 1.0 is an open agent foundation model trained in three simple stages—two lightweight supervised fine‑tuning steps and reinforcement learning—delivering strong agentic performance while releasing full weights, data, and code.
key_points: Trained in only three stages: two SFT phases and RL
No mid‑training, DPO, or on‑policy distillation required
Open release of model weights, data construction, prompts, and training code
Achieves competitive results on agentic benchmarks
why_it_matters: Provides a fully reproducible, open‑source pathway for building powerful agentic AI, lowering barriers for research and enabling community‑driven advancement of open agent intelligence.

headline: Think Less, Locally: Local Preference Learning for Reasoning Compression
tldr: LoCo learns when a reasoning model should stop thinking, cutting chain‑of‑thought length by up to ~45% for math and ~36% for code while keeping or improving accuracy.
key_points: Detects overthinking states from model traces and freezes reasoning prefixes
Regenerates shorter verified continuations and trains with DPO on preference pairs
Reduces completion length 41.7%‑45.4% on math benchmarks and 23.4%‑36.3% on code benchmarks
Maintains or improves accuracy and achieves best AUC on code tasks
Code and model will be open‑sourced on GitHub
why_it_matters: Reduces inference cost of large reasoning models, making them more efficient for real‑world deployment without sacrificing performance, and demonstrates cross‑domain applicability from math to code generation.

headline: DreamX: Video Diffusion Model is a Universal Latent Action Learner
tldr: DreamX repurposes a pretrained video diffusion model to learn compact, embodiment‑invariant latent actions, achieving state‑of‑the‑art results on LARY‑Bench and enabling zero‑shot cross‑embodiment video transfer.
key_points: Extracts latent actions by compressing each video frame 300× (1,200→4 tokens)
Creates a shared action space that works across humans, robots, environments, and parameterizations
Achieves SOTA on LARY‑Bench and supports any‑to‑any and zero‑shot action transfer
Enables policy learning in a compact latent space, lowering computational cost
why_it_matters: Provides a universal, low‑dimensional action representation that decouples dynamics from visual appearance, facilitating transfer learning across embodiments and reducing compute for video‑diffusion‑based policies.

headline: Route Anything: A Study of Model and Policy Routing for General-Purpose AI Systems
tldr: The paper introduces Route Anything, a framework for dynamically routing tasks to specialized AI models and policies, showing that learned routers can improve performance and efficiency across diverse benchmarks.
key_points: Presents a theoretical foundation for optimal model/policy routing under quality‑cost trade‑offs
Evaluates routing on 25 benchmarks covering language, vision, speech, coding, and robotics
Oracle routing beats the best fixed model by 5.4 points; learned routers improve by up to 2.1 points while using 24% less policy time
Achieves an average 8.82× efficiency gain over a reference model
why_it_matters: Effective routing enables heterogeneous AI ecosystems to deliver higher performance with lower computational cost, a critical step toward scalable artificial general intelligence.

headline: Are Frontier VLM Agents Ready to Be Robot Generalists? An Empirical Study with the Embodied Agent Arena
tldr: The paper introduces Embodied Agent Arena to evaluate ten frontier vision‑language models on robot generalist tasks, finding closed‑weight models outperform open‑weight ones, especially in planning and manipulation.
key_points: Embodied Agent Arena tests VLM agents across geometry, spatial reasoning, affordance, task planning, and manipulation using 1,000 cases.
Closed‑weight VLMs lead in all five domains, while open‑weight VLMs show weaker planning and manipulation performance.
Errors often stem from hidden geometric distortions and misidentifying actionable regions, causing subgoal loss or premature task termination.
Additional computation (code repair, self‑review) does not consistently fix failures and can sometimes reverse correct actions.
why_it_matters: Understanding the limits of current VLM agents for embodied robotics highlights gaps in planning and manipulation, guiding future research toward more reliable robot generalists.

headline: Words Caught in the Heart: Simulating Person-Specific Expression for Self-Opaque Clients in Psychotherapy
tldr: Pandora is a new LLM-based framework that simulates psychotherapy clients by explicitly planning expression, achieving higher expression similarity and lower AI-like judgments than prior baselines.
key_points: Models psychological and relational states that update with therapist interventions.
Separates expression planning from language generation using client-specific utterance patterns.
Outperforms five baselines on 115 cases across four counseling datasets.
Reduces AI-like perception from 43.3–67.2% to 7.2% in evaluator study.
why_it_matters: Improving the realism of client simulators can enhance training for therapists and research on therapeutic techniques, ensuring simulated clients reflect individual expression rather than generic, AI-like responses.

headline: YANAMI: A Large-Scale Multimodal Dataset and Benchmark for Multiturn Stateful Interaction
tldr: Introduces YANAMI, a 400K multi-turn multimodal dialogue dataset and benchmark to evaluate models' ability to track and realize evolving dialogue states.
key_points: Contains 400K dialogues, >2M images, and 2.6M turns across four scenarios
Provides YANAMI-Bench with 400 dialogues for systematic evaluation
Fine-tuning BAGEL on YANAMI-400K improves editing, generation, and stateful interaction performance
Current unified multimodal models still struggle with maintaining and visualizing evolving states
why_it_matters: Enables rigorous training and assessment of multimodal models on stateful, multi-turn interactions, a gap in existing benchmarks, driving progress toward more coherent visual dialogue systems.

headline: VidUEU-Agent: A Data-Curation Agent for Multimodal Understanding, Editing, and Unified Tasks
tldr: An automated pipeline converts raw videos into high-quality instruction data, creating the 100K-sample VidUEU-100K dataset that boosts multimodal model performance across tasks.
key_points: Four-stage pipeline filters low-quality shots, extracts keyframes and multimodal signals, and synthesizes instruction samples
Agent can iteratively adjust data distribution based on downstream training results
VidUEU-100K contains 100,000 diverse training samples spanning multiple domains and tasks
Fine‑tuning baseline models on VidUEU-100K yields consistent performance gains on benchmark suites
why_it_matters: It tackles the bottleneck of scarce, costly multimodal instruction data by leveraging abundant video content, enabling more effective training of multimodal AI systems and accelerating research in video‑based understanding and editing.

headline: EvoTeam: Multi-Agent Collaboration via Evolving Teams
tldr: EvoTeam introduces a framework that evolves team organization, interaction rules, and individual agent skills jointly, improving multi-agent system collaboration across heterogeneous tasks.
key_points: Joint evolution of team structure, interaction rules, and agent skills
Maintains a reusable library of teams for context‑specific collaboration
Allows individual skills to be shared across different team configurations
Demonstrated effectiveness on four benchmark tasks
why_it_matters: Better coordination among specialized LLM agents can solve more complex problems, and EvoTeam's approach reduces the need for manual prompt or skill tuning by evolving collaboration itself.

headline: Dory1.0-4B: A Looped Normalized-GPT
tldr: A 4‑billion‑parameter looped language model with elastic depth that can adapt compute budget at inference and outperforms larger models on coding, agentic, and long‑context benchmarks.
key_points: Single checkpoint supports variable inference loops, giving flexible compute budgets.
Pre‑trained on 6 trillion tokens; context length extended to 256K tokens.
Looping improves accuracy and token efficiency, achieving 1.3‑2.5× fewer output tokens on agentic tasks.
Outperforms larger models (Qwen3.5‑9B, Gemma 4 12B, Gemma 4 26B‑A4B) across 12 benchmarks with two or more loops.
Open‑sourced quantized checkpoints in BF16, MXFP8, NVFP4, and GGUF formats.
why_it_matters: Demonstrates that looped, elastic‑depth architectures can deliver higher performance and token efficiency than larger static models, enabling cost‑effective deployment for long‑context and coding applications.
